- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later — suggest adjusting for mean reversion toward historical median.
- When history shows a sharp spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a dampening factor or lagged momentum correction.
- Forecast tends to be too optimistic in the first 3–5 days after a new low or volatile period — reduce initial forecast by 2–5% relative to recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates when true outcome is below 75 — especially after a high, suggesting a “floor effect” — add a minimum threshold adjustment.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often fails to recognize the downward trend — apply a “safety margin” correction to avoid underestimating the drop.
- Forecast often lags the true outcome by 1–3 days — adjust for a 1-day lagged smoothing filter or use a 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — reduce sensitivity to recent outliers (e.g., use rolling median instead of raw mean).
